nodes.name: Co-precipitation and Calcination
nodes.procedure: 0.01 mol of La(NO3)2·6H2O (puriss. p.a., ≥99.0% tritation, Fluka) and 0.01 mol of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (99.999% trace metals basis, Aldrich) were dissolved in deionized water (Milli-Q) and stirred at room temperature until complete dissolution. Then, a solution of 2 M KOH was dropped-in slowly, up to pH ≥13. After the formation of a precipitate, it was washed with deionized water until neutral pH, and finally dried thanks to Buchner filtration. After that, the powder was put in an oven in air at 60 °C for 3 h. Finally, the perovskite powder was obtained after a calcination step in a muffle furnace at 700 °C for 3 h in air.

nodes.description: OER performance using RDE in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The OER performance of the synthesized material was studied in a three-electrode cell set up using a Rotating Disk Electrode (RDE) from Pine instruments... The perovskite catalyst shows a good OER activity, since the OER starts at ca. 1.63 V (vs RHE). The potential E(V) value at 10 mA cm⁻²... the overpotential is 0.43 V... The Tafel slope of 47 mV⋅dec⁻¹ and the j₀ of 1.06⋅10⁻⁹ A cm⁻²

nodes.description: Single CV characterization using C-SPE in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The cyclic voltammogram performed using C-SPE with 0.025 mg of nickel deposited is shown in Fig. 8; cathodic and anodic peaks are visible at about 1.3 V and 1.4 V (vs RHE), respectively... A value of 1.6⋅10⁻⁵ A V and 1.1⋅10⁻⁵ A V were found for anodic and cathodic peak areas, respectively... The fraction of active Ni is about 8.3%... and about 6%

nodes.characterization_summary: LaNiO3 is almost monophasic rhombohedral phase with unit cell parameters a = b = 5.4469 Å, c = 13.1948 Å, volume = 339.030 Å³ and crystallite size 23.9 nm; weak peak at ~44° indicates small NiO impurity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The sample is almost monophasic, as it is shown by comparison with a standard pattern of rhombohedral LaNiO3 (ICDD N◦ 04-013-6811) ... The presence of a weak peak at ca. a 44° can be ascribed to a small impurity of rock salt NiO.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows LaNiO3 morphology as agglomerates and flakes formed by nanometric particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3 represents the SEM images of the LaNiO3 and highlights the perovskite morphology. At low magnification the sample appears as formed by agglomerates and flakes.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM of as-prepared LaNiO3 shows homogeneous crystalline structure with geminate periodicity up to the edge; after KOH treatment unchanged; after OER shows surface disorder with 3-4 nm nano-domains forming mosaic structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HR-TEM images reveal that the perovskite LaNiO3 as prepared exhibits a geminate periodicity ... after the OER, disoriented nanoparticles formed or grew on the surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando XAS at Ni K-edge confirms pristine LaNiO3 has Ni(III) oxidation state matching β-NiOOH reference; at 0.16 V surface Ni reduction to Ni(II); anodic potentials show reversible Ni(III) formation with ~10% surface Ni involved; EXAFS confirms bulk structural stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It is apparent by comparison with the XANES spectra of the reference materials, that for the pristine material the edge energy position is coincident with that of β-NiOOH, which is a standard for Ni(III) ... A fraction of ca. 10% of Ni is obtained, which is in excellent agreement with the values reported above.
